QF.id: AIFM CII Investment Process and Governance_48

question.text: For a Cat II AIF's investment in a mid-cap investee, the FINANCIAL Due Diligence Report (DDR) typically covers the past:

answer.text: At least 3 financial years — with books verification, oral/written representations check, material undisclosed information, tax matters (direct and indirect)

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the PDF, Financial DDR covers at least the past 3 financial years — verification of books, financial statements, business transactions, accuracy of oral/written representations in the IM, material undisclosed information, and direct/indirect tax matters (returns, filings, assessments, potential demands, litigations). The Trap: 3 months is too short. 1 year misses trend. 10 years is excessive (though tax lookback can be up to 10 years in exceptional cases). Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the same 3-year DD standard. XV (Research Analyst) tests DDR concepts too. Manager's Pro-Tip: For Cat II AIFs investing in mature companies, extend Financial DDR to 5 years for tax (GST post-2017 has its own trail) AND legal (review litigation history). Budget 0.5-1% of deal size for DD professional fees.
